Fyrakk the Blazing is the final boss in Amirdrassil, the Dream's Hope and the last boss of World of Warcraft: Dragonflight. Having lost sight of the Incarnates' original mission, Fyrakk now seeks to use the corrupting power of shadowflame to twist Amirdrassil to burn Azeroth to ash and remake it in his own horrifying image. During the battle, the spirits of the Kaldorei within Amirdrassil's seed, killed during the Fourth War and rescued from the Maw, fight to resist Fyrakk's foul influence.

Galactic Combatant's Heraldry is a Competitor's Heraldry optional crafting reagent used by Midnight professions to craft Midnight Season 1 PvP gear. Aside from weapons, usually 3, 4, or 5 are required to craft a single piece of gear. They can be obtained in several different ways. *Looted from PvP strongboxes, such as Illustrious Contender's Strongbox *Looted from War Supply Chests, Alliance bounties, and Horde bounties in War Mode *Bought from Mirvedon in Silvermoon City for 175 Honor *Can be bought and sold on the Auction House

Ghostly Ransom Note was pinned to Alyx's call board on 21 November during Guest Relations. It reads: "Warlords" seems like a reference, but it's actually referring to the final home for dead warlords, Maldraxxus. Atop the Seat of the Primus on the Bleak Redoubt, find the Ghostly Celebration Crate at . The crate is on the exterior portal level (the building's lap, as it were), not on the very top of the structure. Get to Maldraxxus by taking the portal to Oribos in Orgrimmar/Stormwind, then take a flight path to Maldraxxus. If Oribos is bugged and no NPCs are present, go to Dornogal and take the Timeways portal, then go to Ardenweald or Bastion and take a flight path to Maldraxxus. File:Seat

The Gilded Landing is one of the landing areas for broker ferries coming to Tazavesh, the Veiled Market. It serves as both the entry point and starting location for the dungeon. It connects directly to Tazavesh Customs Enforcement. During the war on K'aresh, the Gilded Landing no longer serves as the entry point for Tazavesh as a whole, instead overlooking K'aresh. Both docks are now available, as opposed to only one from . Om'thenai serves as flight master at the end of the dock. Al'dalil is also on the dock, willing to speak with his former cohorts about their previous infiltration of the city. He allows players to relive said events, providing an entrance to the dungeon by way of the ship

Glix Xizzix is a goblin located in the Trade Quarter of the Undercity during . He serves as a barber. He was originally a merchant leading his caravan through Tirisfal Glades some time after the Plaguelands civil war. He was ambushed by the Rot Hide gnolls, who took his wares. He made a deal with Garek Bandarion and Dark Ranger Anya to defeat the gnolls and recover his stolen wares. After the two Forsaken swept through the camp and killed Warlord Torgo, Glix recovered his supplies, and headed to the Undercity, where he started selling his wares to the Forsaken.

The Gnomeregan Army is the principal military force of the kingdom of Gnomeregan on the continent of Khaz Modan. Since the events of the Second War, the gnomish forces have contributed their ingenious weapons to aid the Grand Alliance in its fierce battles against the Horde and other threats to Azeroth, supplying the Alliance army with its most advanced weaponry and war machines. After the fall of Gnomeregan and the loss of eighty percent of their population, it took the gnomes several years to rebuild their military power during their exile in Ironforge. The Gordok Commons are the northern instance in Dire Maul. This area of the city has been taken over by the Gordok, the elite members of the Gordunni ogre clan, and are now the seat of power for King Gordok himself. By tradition, however, whoever slays the king will become the new King Gordok. Following the Fourth War, Zekhan and Rexxar confirmed that despite the deaths of multiple kings, many warriors were still present within the ruins.

Greyguard Elites are humans and worgen of the Gilnean military. Shortly after the war against the Primalists, King Genn Greymane was accompanied by a Greyguard Elite at the Seat of the Aspects in Valdrakken and another one was stationed in the Trade District of Stormwind City. They directed the Alliance adventurer to the Ruins of Gilneas to aid the Gilneans in retaking it. During the Reclamation of Gilneas, they were stationed at Keel Harbor to protect the royal family and later faced the Scarlet Crusaders in Gilneas City among the allied forces. The gutter tribe of kobyss are a group that makes its home within the Salien Gutters; the run off point from the cisterns of the City of Threads. This tribe is noted by the nerubian alchemist, Al'kubian, to be stronger than other kobyss. This strength was later determined to be coming from the various things they were eating, including ascended nerubians. Seeking alchemical reagents, Al'kubian tasked an adventurer with culling some of their numbers, as well as rescuing various nerubians that the kobyss were holding hostage for later consumption. Hall of Fame: Queen Ansurek is a guild feat of strength earned by being among the first two hundred guilds worldwide to defeat Queen Ansurek in Nerub-ar Palace on Mythic difficulty. The Hall of Awakening is located in north-central Ringing Deeps. The zone is the starting zone of the new playable race Earthen. It is the location of the Awakening Machine, the device that awakens earthen from stasis-lock. After the machines of the Ringing Deeps were damaged by the Great Sundering, the Awakening Machine lost its connection to the Manifold and ran on auxiliary power until it eventually shutdown. Without the machine, no new earthen could be awakened and their numbers dwindled over the centuries. Halaan Hawk-Eye is a Skyborne located atop the watchtower of Thendal Village on Zephras Isle. He cannot peer between worlds such as those with the skysight, nor can he draw upon the magic of the ley lines beneath Zephras like others can. He offers adventurers a view of the anchor pylon in the distance, explaining that their magic has grown unstable and inconsistent.

Harrowsdeep was the home of Iridikron and his Primalist forces before and during the War of the Scaleborn, approximately 20,000 years ago. After Iridikron usurped control of the Primalists from Fyrakk, Harrowsdeep became the faction's center of power. Even before the war, it garrisoned a large portion of their proto-dragon and tarasek forces, as well as storing supplies and metalwork for the upcoming battles. It would remain as the heart of Primalist power until the end of the war, where Iridikron was captured in the tunnels below.

A hash'ey is one chosen by one or multiple loa to wield their full power for the good of their people. More than a priest and more akin to a shadow hunter. As a result of the loa's blessings, the hash'ey can live a long life. However, the path of the hash'ey can also be long and arduous, full of trials and perils. As such, the hash'ey is joined by two acolytes known as the hash'ura, who follow them along the path, fight for them, and die for them. Even in death, hash'eys may still command the power of the loa.

Heroic World Tier is an optional difficulty setting in Legion Remix inspired by the Diablo franchise. It is designed to enhance open-world gameplay across the Broken Isles with tougher enemies, 500% experience boost, and greater rewards. Participating in this difficulty is as simple as activating it from the Console of Infinite Chaos, near Eternus at the Infinite Bazaar in Dalaran. Enemies will have more health, more damage, and occasionally Affix-like buffs, empowering their difficulty and rewards: 500% more experience, Bronze, and Infinite Power. There are four affixes. Infinite Knowledge is the warband-wide currency gained during Legion Remix. It increases the amount of Infinite Power that drops from all sources for each Timerunner on the warband. Knowledge increases gained power at two rates: * IK 1–20: 5% per level (100% total) * IK 21–36: 3.125% per level (150% total) Infinite Knowledge is only awarded from achievements. The overall cap is 36 Infinite Knowledge, and any achievements that would award Knowledge above that level will instead automatically grant a Bronze Cache.

Jewelcrafters (or jewelers and gemwrights) are artisans who unlock the surprising power in precious stones, creating potent jewelry and trinkets. They craft rings, amulets, and other objects of known mystical power, but they also cut gems to fit in socketed items like weapons and pieces of armor, granting those pieces of equipment unique properties. A talented jewelcrafter can count on a demand for their services in crafting special items, improving equipment, and shaping rare gems. They often rely on miners to gather ores and gems. With enough patience, expert jewelcrafters can carefully carve draenite crystals to reveal deep blue or purple shades.

The Kaja'Coast is a goblin kaja'mite mine located on the western shore of Zuldazar. While initially established and run by the Bilgewater Cartel with Zandalari permission, it was briefly taken over by the Venture Company and Darkfuse Enforcement. Venture and Darkfuse blew up a mountain sacred to the loa Pa'ku to mine more kaja'mite, angering the Zandalari. Once Bilgewater regained control the Zandalari began to watch them more closely and ensure that they made things right. Players unlock access to the area halfway through the third chapter of the Undermine(d) campaign by opening up a rocket drill at Slam Central Station in Undermine.

Kaqiata is a dead tuskarr located in Brackenhide Brambles in the Azure Span. She was the mother of Rowie. She went with her fellow tuskarr to a hunt, but was killed by the Brackenhide gnolls. When the adventurer found her body and called upon her spirit, instead of crossing over Kaqiata resolved to empower Brena's Totem to fight against the decay-corrupted gnolls. Brena then summoned her to help destroy the Twisted Ancient, after which Brena thanked her and released all the spirits to be with Karkut.

Kindo'jan was a forest troll who once led the Amani tribe and their empire. He was the first Amani hash'ey, having received the blessings of the four most powerful loa of Zul'Aman, Akil'zon, Halazzi, Jan'alai, and Nalorakk, as well as the minor loa of the region. He was so beloved of Akil'zon that, from then on, the loa became not only the Loa of Victory but also the loa of the Amani tribe and its leaders. Having lived a long life spanning many generations, Kindo'jan notably established the order of the Loa Speakers, formalizing the worship rituals that are still practiced in modern times.
